name: Overload Damper
desc: A cascade breaker pulled from Domain-era fortress emitters. When a flux grid buckles, it dumps the surge into a sacrificial lattice instead of the ship's systems, buying the few seconds a conventional grid never gets.

name: Nanolattice Regenerator
desc: A colony of dormant repair nanites seeded through the armor matrix. In battle they wake and knit cracked plating back together, starving themselves as they go; by the end of an engagement they are spent, and they regrow in the hold before the next.

name: Cryo-Flux Exchanger
desc: Supercooled exchange loops threaded behind the shield emitters. Hard flux that normally has nowhere to go is siphoned into the loops and bled away, even while the shield holds.

name: Temporal Capacitor
desc: A sealed chronometric capacitor that stores a sliver of the ship system's charge cycle and releases it early. The engineers refuse to explain how, and the warranty specifically excludes complaints about causality.

name: Phase Coil Tuner
desc: A Tri-Tachyon calibration rig that keeps phase coils resonant between activations, so slipping into p-space costs less and the coils need far less time to settle.

name: Point Defense Integrator
desc: A fire control node that slaves every light mount to the point defense network. Small guns track missiles and fighters as eagerly as a dedicated PD battery.

name: Hangar Microforge
desc: A nanoforge writ small and bolted into the flight deck. It prints replacement airframes on demand, keeping the launch tubes full long after a normal carrier would run dry.

name: Missile Autoforge
desc: A compact fabricator that turns scrap and stored propellant into fresh warheads in the middle of a battle. It is slow, but it never stops working.

name: Vent Thrusters
desc: Venting ducts rerouted through the main drive. Dumped flux becomes thrust, so a venting ship surges forward instead of sitting still and waiting to be shot.

name: Fire Control Equalizer
desc: An adaptive targeting suite that pushes short-ranged guns out to the edge of their envelope with predictive fire and stabilised optics.
